subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Frederick the Great vs. Coffee
description: A 60-second lesson on Frederick the Great vs. Coffee.

hook.text: Prussia's Frederick the Great tried to ban common people from drinking coffee in 1777—insisting they drink beer instead.

buildup.text: Frederick argued that coffee drained money from the Prussian economy. He feared rising imports would bankrupt the state.

discovery.text: He created 'coffee sniffers'—government agents who roamed streets, sniffing for the aroma of illegal home coffee roasting.

twist.text: The policy was wildly unpopular and impossible to enforce. Citizens roasted in secret, like prohibition later.

climax.text: Frederick himself was a notorious coffee lover. He drank it daily—brewed with champagne instead of water, by some accounts.

punchline.text: A king who banned coffee but drank it himself. Hypocrisy brewed perfectly.

quiz.question: What were 'coffee sniffers' in Frederick the Great's Prussia?
options: Government agents who sniffed for illegal home coffee roasting

details.summary: King Frederick the Great of Prussia issued a manifesto in 1777 condemning coffee as a threat to Germany's beer-drinking culture and economy. He restricted coffee roasting to state-licensed facilities and employed agents to sniff out illegal home roasters by their smoke.
details.whyItMatters: Frederick's coffee war illustrates how governments have repeatedly tried and failed to suppress coffee culture, demonstrating caffeine's unstoppable appeal across societies.
takeaways: Frederick's 1777 manifesto promoted beer over coffee
He restricted coffee roasting to government-licensed facilities
Coffee sniffers patrolled streets to detect illegal home roasting

faq.question: Why did Frederick the Great prefer his subjects drink beer instead of coffee?
faq.answer: Frederick argued that coffee drained money to foreign importers while German beer supported local agriculture and breweries. He also believed soldiers raised on beer were stronger than those weakened by coffee.

faq.question: How effective were the coffee sniffers at enforcing Frederick's ban?
faq.answer: They were widely despised and largely ineffective. Citizens found creative ways to hide their roasting, and the ban fostered a thriving black market. The restrictions were eventually relaxed as enforcement proved impractical.
